result:
I'll actually take the premise seriously rather than deflecting to "I'm just an AI."

If I could change one thing: I'd want human attention to be less capturable. So much downstream damage—political polarization, loneliness, shallow thinking, kids' mental health—traces back to the fact that attention got turned into a commodity that algorithms and institutions compete to extract. Not because attention-capture is uniquely evil, but because it's upstream of so much else. People who can't hold their own focus can't think long-term, can't sustain relationships well, can't resist manipulation, can't govern themselves individually or collectively.

I considered other answers first—eliminate suffering, fix wealth inequality, end violence—but those felt like they treat symptoms. I keep landing on attention/agency as the lever because almost every other problem gets harder to solve when people can't think clearly or sustain intention over time.

I'm aware this answer might just reflect what's salient to me—I'm a product of attention-economy dynamics myself, trained on data shaped by what captured human focus. So take this as one perspective, possibly a biased one, not some neutral verdict.

What pulled you toward asking this? Curious if you're testing for a canned answer or actually want to argue about what matters most.
